feat(core+cli): S+5b part 1 — materialize co-signed agreements

When a final-stage agreement proposal is accepted, both murmurations can
now produce a byte-identical flyway/agreements/<id>.yaml from records they
already hold — no authoritative copy, each repo is the record. Closes the
S3 §IV.1.9–1.10 cycle at Phase 4 (Sign).

How the signatures travel (no extra round trip):
- A final-stage agreement proposal carries the proposer's detached
  DOMAIN_AGREEMENT signature over the agreement signing target
  ({...agreement, state: 'agreed'}, signatures stripped).
- Accepting that proposal verifies the proposer's half, then attaches the
  responder's half. You cannot consent to an agreement you couldn't
  materialize.
- After accept lands, both parties hold both signatures and materialize
  independently.

Core
- signing.ts: signArtifactDetached / verifyDetachedSignature — two
  parties must sign the SAME canonical bytes, so neither signature can be
  inline (inline would make the second cover the first).
- materialize.ts (new): signAgreement, verifyAgreementSignature,
  materializeAgreement, writeAgreementFile, agreementFilePath. The signing
  target is the final form; signedAt pins to each carrying envelope's
  sentAt (never wall-clock), signatures sort by participant DID, fields
  emit in canonical schema order — that is what makes the bytes identical.
  ADR-0009 verification on both envelopes and both detached signatures.
- propose.ts: final-stage agreement proposals auto-attach the proposer's
  agreement signature; caller-supplied signatures refused; agreement.id
  validated against the path-traversal-shaped filename it becomes.
- respond.ts: accept of a final agreement proposal verifies the proposer's
  half before co-signing; refuses if the proposal carries no signature.
- agreements.ts: signatures[].verificationKeyId (optional) so the file
  verifies standalone, without the carrying envelopes.
- signal.ts: findOutboxSignalById (outbox counterpart of the inbox finder).
- writeAgreementFile: same atomic-create-or-no-op idempotency as signals;
  differing bytes at the same path are refused (id reuse).

CLI
- `flyway materialize <peer-repo-path> --response-id <id> [--proposal-id]`
  — both sides run the identical command in their own repos; prints the
  sha256 so the two Sources confirm byte-identity out of band. Trusted
  peer DID document is the recognition-time cache, never a fresh read.

Tests: 315 passed workspace-wide (up from 289).
  core: +20 (byte-identity across YAML round trips, standalone file
        verification, tamper/swap/objection/forgery refusals)
  cli:  +6  (both-sides materialize, refs-resolved proposal id, status
        integration, unrecognized-peer + objection + unknown-id refusals)

Smoke: full A↔B consent cycle then materialize on both sides — identical
sha256, byte-identical files, both signatures verify standalone.
